title: I keep reliving the same gas station night shift. Each loop, a man outside gets closer.
transcript:
I keep reliving the same gas station night shift. Each loop, a man outside gets closer. The bell over the door rang at midnight. Again.

Same trucker. Same black coffee. Same question. "Bathroom key?" I slid it across the counter, and he walked to the back, whistling. He never brings it back. He never comes out.

This was my fifth time living this night. At three, the lights die, and I wake up at the register at midnight.

And every loop, the man at pump four gets closer. No car. Hood up. Facing the store. The first night he stood out by the road. Last loop, he was at the ice machine, right outside the door.

So this time, I acted. At two fifty, I locked the front door and grabbed the bat from under the counter.

At two fifty-nine, he was at the glass. He pressed his palm flat against it and spoke, muffled. "Every time, you lock me out."

Then he pointed. Past me. Toward the back hall.

Behind me, a key turned in the bathroom lock. A door creaked open. And that whistling, slow and happy, coming closer.

"Let me in," the man at the glass begged. "He's done this to you four times."

I reached for the lock. My hand was shaking.

The whistling stopped. Right behind me.
